title: Conversation Microsurgeon — idea & rough PRD
content:
Context:
Small scratchpad for an experiment-lean feature that surgically edits, reorders, or compresses portions of an in-session conversation to reduce token cost while preserving semantic fidelity where it matters. Working name: Conversation Microsurgeon.

Problem statement:
- Apps (assistants, chat UIs, task flows) accumulate long histories; cost and latency increase with naive replay.
- Existing approaches: naive truncation, semantic summarization (lossy), explicit user-curation. Each has tradeoffs: latency, hallucination risk, loss of instruction-level detail.
- Need a fine-grained operator: keep the bits that change decisions, compress or elide the rest.

High-level idea:
- Instead of one global summary, identify 'surgical edits' on a turn-by-turn basis: remove boilerplate, compress repetitive confirmations, retain decision-critical utterances.
- Provide a compact representation: a mix of preserved turns, compressed stubs, and anchors linking to full turns if needed (on-demand fetch).
- Operate at the proxy/service layer (not modifying app UX initially) so we can A/B easily.

Goals (measurable):
- Reduce token replay by 40–70% for long-lived sessions (10+ turns) on target apps (task assistants, knowledge workers).
- Maintain task success KPI within 95% of baseline (per-app evals).
- Add <= 15ms median overhead to request path (target: 5–10ms).

Non-goals:
- Not a replacement for full convo summarization features or explicit user edit flows.
- Not trying to invent new LLMs for compression; leverage model+heuristics.

User stories (initial):
- As a product engineer, I want token replay to be reduced for long sessions, so my app's API bill decreases without visible regressions to users.
- As an assistant user, I want the assistant to remember important decisions even if older turns are compressed.
- As an SRE, I want the system to be revertible and provide deterministic logs/anchors to reconstruct full context for debugging.

Proposed design components:
1) Turn classifier (cheap)
   - Lightweight model/heuristic that marks turns as: KEEP, COMPRESS, SKIP, ANCHOR.
   - Features: turn length, role (user/system), presence of instructions, named entities, task triggers, edit distance to recent turns, repetition score.
   - Implementation: small transformer classifier (distil or distilled embedding+MLP) or rule set seeded by patterns.

2) Compression operator (compress)
   - For turns marked COMPRESS, apply one of: one-line extractive, canonical stub ("user confirmed X"), or compact embed+proxy-repr.
   - Use model-assisted extractive compression via prompt to a small cheap model (e.g., 1.5B or hosted distilled endpoint) — or deterministic heuristics for templates.

3) Anchor pointers (deferred fetch)
   - For ANCHORed turns, include a stable id + small descriptor in replay. The full roundtrip can be fetched by the proxy (or retrieved from storage) if the model requests more details (fallback).

4) Safety & fidelity checks
   - Build a quick QA step: after constructing compressed context, run a small probe prompt that checks for lost directives ("Does assistant have instruction X?") — treat as a guardrail.
   - Keep a fail-open policy: if probe uncertain, revert to denser context.

5) Observability & rollback
   - Tokenized before/after token counts, per-turn labels, compression ratio, task-eval binary.
   - Store original turns for 30 days (configurable), redaction/hashing options for PII.

Operational modes (config flags per-customer):
- aggressive (max compression, higher risk)
- conservative (prefer KEEP/ANCHOR, lower savings)
- on-demand (compress only when token budget exceeded)

Metrics to track:
- request_token_replay_before, request_token_replay_after, compression_ratio
- task_success_rate_by_app, latency_p50/p95, probe_failure_rate
- fallback_rate (how often fetch full turn during generation)

Experiments / rollout plan:
- Phase 0: internal A/B with synthetic long sessions and canned user flows. Goal: sanity check latency, basic fidelity on known prompts.
- Phase 1: opt-in beta for a small set of self-serve customers (product-hosted-api customers flagged in config). Collect usage and user-reported regressions.
- Phase 2: broader default for new sessions on low-risk workloads (chat summaries, auto-responders).

Acceptance criteria for safe rollout:
- <5% drop in per-app task-specific evaluation (define app-specific evals beforehand).
- median additional latency <15ms, p95 <50ms.
- fallback rate <15% on conservative mode.

Technical risks & mitigation:
- Risk: Probe prompts themselves add cost/latency. Mitigate: run cheap heuristic probes first; use probes only on turns likely to carry instructions.
- Risk: Hallucinated compressed stubs. Mitigate: anchor + on-demand fetch and aggressive logging; provide user-visible indicators in product later.
- Risk: PII leakage if storing originals. Mitigate: default redaction, customer opt-out, short retention window, integrate KMS.

Implementation sketch (milestones):
- Week 0–2: prototype turn classifier rules & metrics harness; run offline on existing anonymized session traces to measure potential savings.
- Week 3–6: implement compression operator and anchor proto; simulate end-to-end in proxy (no live traffic).
- Week 7–10: internal AB test with small internal apps; add probes and observability dashboards.
- Week 11–16: opt-in beta per-customer, collect telemetry, iterate.

Open questions / decisions:
- Where to run the classifier/compressor? (proxy vs edge vs client). Proxy preferred for rollout speed, but edge reduces latency — need benchmark.
- Which cheap model to use for compression? distil-bison-ish or custom 1.3B? Cost vs quality tradeoff.
- How to express anchors to LLMs reliably (best prompt patterns)? Need a few prompt experiments.
- How aggressively to redact stored turns by default? Legal/Privacy input required.

Quick todo list:
- [ ] Get anonymized session traces from Product (Priya)
- [ ] Spike rule-based classifier on 10k sessions (Zane)
- [ ] Draft probe-prompt templates (Mika)
- [ ] Wire minimal telemetry to Datadog/Console (Evan)
- [ ] Legal check: retention defaults + PII redaction (ask Security/Compliance)

Notes to self (brain dump):
- Could integrate with prefix/KV cache: compressed stubs can be cached as keys; skipping could reduce KV churn.
- Idea: user-facing "recall" action to expand anchors inline in UI — good for research and product adoption.
- Could pair with model routing: aggressive compression -> route to cheaper model; conservative -> route to full model.
- Consider a hybrid: per-turn compression but allow windowed dense context for N most recent turns.
